annotations.text:
THE SYSTEM — built and running in the app.

Type: Zilla Slab 600/700 for anything that names something; IBM Plex Sans 400/600 for everything else. Self-hosted, so the shell still reads offline in a gym.

Colour: one neutral ramp (paper, surface, ink, ink-2, ink-3, rule) plus a single burnt orange. Nothing else is coloured, so the video thumbnails are the only real colour on any screen.

Shape: 3px radii, hairline rules, 2px rules for structure. Boxes are ruled entries, not floating cards.

Size: body 15px (was 14), summaries 14px, nothing under 12px — this gets read outdoors by a 9-year-old.

LEVELS ARE FORM, NOT COLOUR.

The old green / amber / red badges read as safe / caution / danger. Level 3 is not a warning, it is further along — so the level is three filled segments plus the numeral, and it survives being printed, dimmed or colour-blind.

HOME
The category grid became a numbered contents list with dot leaders — full-width rows are easier to hit one-handed, and the blurb now fits under each entry.

Search, then Start here, then the contents: three jobs in priority order.

CATEGORY
“Where are you?” sits above the levels — the first real question on a court, and Indoor court is the once-a-week resource.

Levels are ruled sections, not boxed cards. L1 open, L2/L3 closed.

SKILL DETAIL
Key points are numbered entries above the prose: the 9-year-old reads the video and these, and nothing else.

The video keeps square corners so the thumbnail reads as a plate in the page, not a sticker on it.

DARK — SAME MARKUP
Identical HTML; only the token values change. There is not a single dark: variant in the codebase, which is why the two themes cannot drift apart.

This is the version that gets used in an evening gym.

SEARCH
Searches names, summaries and tags, so “home” or “solo” work as queries.

Results carry category, level and the level meter — placeable without opening them.

CONTENTS
The index at the back of the book: every skill, no thumbnails, nothing to scroll past.

This is the screen for seeing the whole map at once.

The three directions, kept for the record. B was chosen and carried through — with one change: the warm paper tone was dropped for a neutral ramp, so dark mode is a straight token swap rather than a second palette.

A and C are not built. If the kids react badly to B, A is the one to try next: same structure, much louder.
